messages:
maya: Heads up — cedar-2 internal launch planned next Tue 10am PT. Staging perf suggests ~2.8x tokens/sec vs cedar-1. Can infra ops do a quick sanity-check on GPU-hour and regional risk?

liam: Do we have avg tokens/request and expected rps shape? from staging logs avg_tokens ~ 78, p95 request rate ~ 110 rps per shard.

maya: avg_tokens 78, peak expected rps global ~ 5.5k (we're assuming PLG spike + marketing).

liam: rough calc: peak_tokens/sec = 5.5k * 78 = 429k tok/s. current cedar-1 capacity served ~150k tok/s on our dedicated pool. so ~2.86x which matches perf delta.

liam: throughput per GPU (cedar-2, fp16, seq=512) measured ~20k tok/s on p4d-type. GPUs needed (no buffer) = 429k/20k = 21.45 -> 22 GPUs. with 30% buffer -> ~29 GPUs.

maya: ok 29 GPUs peak. what about GPU-hours & cost for a 6h launch window vs steady state day?

liam: GPU-hours = GPUs * hours. for 6h peak = 29 * 6 = 174 GPU-hours. if we need 24/7 tail at 40% of peak for 24h: steady = 0.4*29=11.6 -> 12 GPUs * 24 = 288 GPU-hours. total day = 174 + 288 = 462 GPU-hours.

liam: cost estimate: assume $2.40/hr per GPU on reserved fleet equivalent -> 462 * 2.4 = $1,108.8 per day (launch day). If we instead route to on-demand cloud GPUs avg $3.6/hr -> $1,663.2

aj: region constraints: asia-east has almost no spare p4d capacity during business hours. we should plan routing to us-west / eu-west as fallback. cross-region KV cache misses will spike latency for long chat flows.

ops-bot: automated-projection-bot: Projected peak_tokens/sec=429000; recommended_capacity_with_buffer=429000*1.5=643500 -> recommended_gpus= ceil(643500/20000)=33 GPUs. Note: does not account for quantization uplift.

sre-bot: infra-alert: current reserved pool spare=8 p4d-equivalent GPUs in us-west, 4 in eu-west, 0 in asia-east. Autoscale policy max burst configured 20 GPUs.

eva: Mitigations we should consider (fast):
- enable int8 quantization profile for cedar-2 (staging shows ~1.8x throughput uplift)
- dynamic batching bump for 80-300ms windows for TTL-heavy endpoints
- fallback routing: long sequences -> cedar-1 or smaller context variant to reduce tok/sec
- pre-warm KV cache in us-west 1hr before launch (warm prefix cache for top 200 prompts)

liam: if int8 gives 1.8x, effective tok/s per GPU -> 36k -> recommended_gpus = ceil(429k/36k)=12 -> with buffer 18. big difference. we should validate quality delta first.

aj: networking note: cross-region routing cost ~+15% egress and 80-120ms added p95 latency. for conversational apps that do many short calls that kills UX. consider regional sticky routing for high-latency-sensitive customers.

maya: action items:
- liam: finalize GPU counts for 3 scenarios (no-quant, int8, fallback) by EOD
- eva: perf/QA to validate int8 quality on 500 eval prompts by EOD+1
- aj: propose routing policy for asia fallback + cost delta
- infra: can we temporarily raise autoscale max burst to 40 GPUs for the window?

liam: tentative numbers I will post in a quick table: 
```
scenario | peak_gpus | gpu-hrs (6h peak + 24h tail) | est daily cost (reserved $2.4/hr)
no-quant | 29 | 462 | $1,108.8
int8 | 18 | 288 | $691.2
fallback | 22 | 350 | $840.0
```

maya: +1 on that table. also need to check reserved commit utilization vs new purchase. Finance sign-off probable if launch lifts MRR.

ops-bot: Preflight checklist status: capacity_quota_check=PASS; registry_models_ok=PASS; autoscale_limit=20 (requested increase pending).

sre-bot: I'll open a quick infra ticket to request autoscale max bump to 40 for 10:00-16:00 PT next Tue. tagging @infra-oncall for approval.

maya: thanks all. will sync with product marketing to get SLO for the first 24h. I'll update this thread after the infra ticket is created. :thumbsup:

liam: queued — I'll attach the perf numbers + links to staging logs in the infra ticket.

aj: note for follow-up: if we route asia traffic out-of-region, send a note to enterprise customers (latency change) and enable opt-out.

maya: closing loop — filing the rollout plan in product/launch and will ping infra ticket link here when ready.
